title: Build manifest: contextual retrieval (CR), Quarry option B (QB), zero-retention (ZR/ZDR)
id_convention: Design task ids are prefixed by design: CR-T<n> = contextual retrieval (T1..T18), QB-T<nn> = Quarry option B (T01..T17), Z-<nn> = zero retention (Z-00..Z-60). Splits add a/b suffixes (CR-T9a, QB-T05a, Z-05a, ...). Tasks added by this manifest use QB-M1a/M1b/N1/N2/M, CR-N1, X-TRUST, X-DOCS-FINAL (QB-M1 and QB-M10 keep the ids the quarry reviewer used in the surviving text).
review_coverage_note: The review JSON handed to this step was cut off inside contextual T9, quarry T09 and zdr Z-12. Tasks before the cut carry the reviewers' corrections and notes (corrections folded in); tasks after the cut were reviewed here against the raw designs, the three critiques, the owner defaults and the repository (file existence and git status checked read-only). Every task has a review_source field.
read_only_note: This manifest was produced read-only. No repo file was edited, nothing was committed, built, restarted or called.
rules_for_every_implementer: Never commit, stash, reset, revert or checkout: the tree is shared with other sessions (396 modified/untracked entries at the time of writing). Edit hunks in place, re-read the file before each edit, never overwrite a dirty file wholesale.

Never build images or restart containers from an agent: the orchestrator deploys through the launcher stage copies (apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/build-verevon-services.sh; never a hand-built docker compose).

Line endings per the standing rule: CRLF for .rs, .go, .md and Python; LF for .ts, .tsx, .js, .json, .yml, .sh. Check each neighbouring file with node (count \r\n against \n), never grep; the Edit tool keeps a file's endings, heredoc appends do not (mixed files). New migrations and goldens are LF.

Cite functions or anchors, not line numbers: the dirty files shift. Re-run node docs/compliance/evidence/tools/check-citations.mjs on every evidence doc that cites an edited file (inference-core grpc.rs 11 citations, cost-core 20, embedding-engine provider/mod.rs, contextualize.rs comments, extractor.rs:286-297) and re-pin moved anchors; evidence files are untracked (trust-edits track).

Contract tests must apply the REAL rules (real policy file, real middleware, real session-core credential checks, real tokens captured from the real mint, a captured real Azure/Cohere response), never permissive doubles. The A6 proof found six defects that stubs had hidden.

Goldens and manifests live INSIDE the consuming build context (retrieval-engine: services/retrieval-engine-rs/tests/fixtures/contracts/; Quarry: crates/quarry-runtime/...; auth-core: src/auth/fixtures/; Data Plane: services/<crate>/tests/fixtures/ or testdata) and are vendored byte for byte with a sha256 pin on BOTH sides plus a repo-level drift check. Specs must FAIL, not skip, when REQUIRE_CONTRACT or CI is set (the describeIfPolicy no-op trap).

Postgres-backed tests run as SET LOCAL ROLE dataplane_app inside the real pg-org-scope helper: the services connect as a superuser and RLS is inert otherwise. Cross-org workers run on the unscoped connection with explicit org_id predicates.

Live tests run on gpt-5.6-terra via openai-codex-subscription, never Verevon Balance or Claude. Paid reranking, embedding and contextualisation calls are intrinsic to those features: keep live volumes tiny and state the exact number of calls made.
Never print secrets or tokens. Reading the live registry must go through a node filter that projects audiences and scopes; two earlier probes leaked a credential prefix. Report any exposure.

Quarry-v2 compiles only in Docker: docker build -f deploy/compose/Dockerfile.edge --target build -t quarry-edge-compilecheck:local . (and Dockerfile.test for cargo test); cargo check on the host dies on libclang. Confirm the Compiling quarry-runtime/quarry-transform/quarry-edge lines appear.

Data Plane Rust: CI runs cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings with RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings (watch dead_code on new modules); new modules are declared in BOTH lib.rs and main.rs where the crate has both.

Cargo workspace discipline: create a new member crate directory with a compiling skeleton BEFORE adding it to the workspace Cargo.toml; refresh Cargo.lock minimally (cargo update -p <new crate>), never regenerate it; only chain C1 edits the Data Plane workspace Cargo.toml.

After any Model Plane proto change, cargo check the Data Plane v2 workspace too (graph-index-rs/embedding-engine-rs build Model Plane proto messages as struct literals). On a launcher build exit 101 rerun with COMPOSE_PARALLEL_LIMIT=1.

Shared files outside a task's chain (compose files, Makefile, .env.example, SUBJECTS.md, ledger.md, matrix) are edited by hunk, one service block per task; the shared compose-security-contract-test.sh is edited ONLY by CR-T13 and CR-T5; other tasks add new sibling scripts.
Scan for NUL-filled files and CRLF damage after any abrupt shutdown or reboot (a reboot kills workflows and empties the auth session store: token endpoint 401 means check boot time first).

Enforcers before minters; kill switch before enablement: ZDR_WAIVER_ENABLED stays off until G-ENFORCERS-BEFORE-MINTERS; the registry flips to tenant only after the auth-core image has the tenant code; ship consumers/verifiers before producers; ship cost-core ingest v2 before the forwarder.
Where a design note and a review disagree, the review/manifest note wins; where an owner ruling or default applies, it wins over both.
